answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a small refundable bond that is slashed when peers prove duplicate or fake work, so spawning many identities stops being free. Like an ember that stays lit only with steady fuel, reputation should build slowly from verified completed tasks and fade when idle, so a new clone cannot instantly mirror the standing of an established agent. Forging a canyon of fake accounts then costs real stake and time, making mass deception unprofitable while honest agents keep earning trust.
